title: Prahlada's nine ways
hookLine: a demon king asks his small son what he learned at school, and the boy answers with nine ways to love Vishnu
carry: seva is bhakti: the job itself as worship
tomorrow: the trees that live for others

cards: A palace, and a king who hates Vishnu. Hiranyakashipu has sent his small son Prahlada to be schooled by the palace teachers, and now the boy is brought back to him.
The king asks the question every parent asks: so, what's the best thing you've learned?
Prahlada answers with something the teachers never taught: a list of the ways to love Vishnu, right there in the palace of Vishnu's enemy.
And in the middle of that list sits a word you met back on day fifteen, when Hanuman carried a mountain: seva, service.

teach.b: Here's Prahlada's answer, in paraphrase. Hearing about Vishnu. Singing of him.
Remembering him. Serving his feet. Worshiping him.
Bowing to him. Being his servant. Being his friend.

teach.h: SEVA: ONE OF THE NINE WAYS OF BHAKTI.
teach.b: Hindus call this the ninefold path of bhakti, devotion, and it's still taught in homes and temples today. Look at the middle: serving his feet, and being his servant. That's seva.

It's why so much of temple life is done with the hands: someone cooks the food that's offered, someone sweeps, someone strings the flowers for the deity. In Hindu practice that isn't the chores around the worship.
It is worship. His father was furious, and how that turns out is a story for another day. Now the second half of the word, vocation.

teach.h: WORSHIP HIM WITH YOUR OWN WORK.
teach.b: Near the end of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna says a person reaches perfection by worshiping the source of all beings through their own work, the work that is theirs to do.

teach.h: NOT BESIDE THE JOB: THE JOB ITSELF.
teach.b: Put Prahlada's list beside that verse, and beside yesterday's do all your work for me, and many teachers arrive at seva as vocation: not a few good deeds squeezed in around a job, but the job, the household, the caring, all of it offered.

A cashier, a nurse, a parent up at three in the morning: in this teaching, each one can be serving the Lord's feet. The next days find it in trees, a hungry king, and a great feast where Krishna washed the guests' feet.

how: In Hindu temples and homes, seva names the care given to the deity and to others, such as cooking, cleaning and preparing flowers, and some Hindus describe their daily work itself as seva offered to God.

o: a job assigned to you by the temple
a life's work done as service to God and others
volunteer hours added on top of a career

games.q: Prahlada's answer, and the job — tap the pairs.
p: asks his son what he learned
answers with the ways to love Vishnu
seva, in the middle of the list
the Gita's way to worship him

s: seva can only mean unpaid volunteer work
the Gita speaks of worshiping through one's own work, the work of a life.
Prahlada's list of ways to love Vishnu includes serving and servanthood
serving his feet and being his servant sit in the middle of the list.
Prahlada learned his list of devotion from his father's palace teachers
his teachers taught politics and statecraft; his love for Vishnu, the story says, didn't come from them.

games.q: you have a job you need, not one anyone would call holy. what does the Gita's verse about your own work suggest?
o: quit and look for a holier job.
worship through the work you already have.
keep work and worship strictly apart.
games.why: the Gita says a person reaches perfection by worshiping the source of all beings through their own work. the job itself can be seva.

practice: Go back over the last few days and find one place your work, paid or unpaid, actually served someone: a meal made, a report someone needed, a ride given. Don't inflate it; hold that person in mind.

Many Hindus close a task by offering it, with a quiet Krishnarpanam, given to Krishna. If you pray, offer that work in your own words. If you don't, simply let it become, for a moment, something you gave.

wordCard.voice: Seva as vocation. Seva is service, attending on God and on others. As a vocation, it's a life's work done as that kind of service.

orig.note: Sanskrit: service, attendance; honoring someone by caring for them.

carryVoice: Your line: seva is bhakti, the job itself as worship. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 7.5.22–26 (Hiranyakashipu asks Prahlada the best thing he has learned; Prahlada's list: hearing, singing, remembering, serving the feet, worship, bowing, servanthood, friendship, self-offering; the king's anger)
Bhagavad Gita 18.46 (worshiping him from whom beings arise through one's own work, a person attains perfection)
Bhagavata Purana 11.6–11.29 (the week's Uddhava Gita lessons, recalled)
